newsitem.title: USA: New York takes, restores baby parked in stroller.
newsitem.headline: New York takes, restores baby parked in stroller.

text.p: A Family Court judge ruled on Tuesday that a baby placed in foster care should be returned to her mother, a visiting Danish actress who left the child outside in a stroller while eating in a New York restaurant.

Annette Sorensen, 30, parked 14-month-old Liv Sorensen outside the window of an East Village restaurant on Saturday night while she and the baby's father, Exavier Wardlaw, 49, a Disney Co. production assistant who lives in Brooklyn, were eating inside, police said.
But two people saw the infant crying and called police.
The couple were arrested after a dispute with police. They were charged with endangering the welfare of a child and disorderly conduct, according to a complaint filed in Manhattan Criminal Court.

The infant was turned over to the city's Administration for Children's Services, which monitors the welfare of minors. She was examined at a local hospital, which found no signs of abuse, a spokeswoman for the agency said.
Sorensen spent two days in jail. On Tuesday she went to New York City's Family Court to get her baby back, an attorney for the father said.

A lawyer for the Administration of Children's Services told reporters after the hearing, "The parties have agreed that the child will be paroled to the mother under the conditions that ACS monitor (Sorensen's) home to make sure it is a safe environment and also to interview all individuals living in that home."
The judge, Sheldon Rand, also ruled that the baby must never be left alone with Sorensen and another adult must always be present.
The agency spokeswomen said mother and child should be reunited by late Wednesday afternoon.
Sorensen, who is staying with friends in the East Village, has a ticket to return to Copenhagen on May 27.
David Kirsch, Wardlaw's attorney, said Sorensen had gotten into trouble for doing something quite common in her homeland.
"In Copenhagen, parents always leave their children outside when they are in a restaurant so that the child can get fresh air," he said.
Kirsch said Sorensen had been in the United States less than 48 hours when her daughter was taken from her.
"It's not like she was leaving her child and abandoning the baby," he said. "They certainly didn't deserve to have the baby taken away from them. This is too drastic."
She and Wardlaw are due in Criminal Court next Monday. She must return to Family Court on Wednesday regarding the custody of her child.
